title: A 365-Day Chronological Bible Reading Plan
about: The plan reads Scripture in the order events happened (or, for prophets and letters, when they were most likely written), tracing one covenant of grace from creation to new creation and its fulfillment in Christ (Luke 24:27; WCF 7.5–6). Each group notes where it places a book whose date is uncertain.
**Plan days** are numbered 1–365. Narrative days stay at three chapters or fewer, every epistle day is exactly one chapter, and psalms marked with "+" are short add-ons tied to the event.

**Supplementary readings** are marked **S** with the passage in italics. Together with the plan, they cover every chapter of the Bible. Each one sits at its best-guess chronological place and groups together consecutive chapters of one book that the plan skips at that point, so some are long (Leviticus 17–27, Psalms 58–71). Where a supplement belongs between two chapters read on the same plan day, it is listed right after that day and its note says so. In the Gospels, supplements are the parallel accounts, listed right after the day that reads the same events. They are optional and untimed: read them alongside the plan, save them for a second year, or skip them.

WCF (Westminster Confession of Faith) and WSC (Westminster Shorter Catechism) notes point to readings that anchor a doctrine in the Westminster Standards. Every section of the Confession has at least one of its 1647 proof texts in the plan days.

groups.title: Beginnings: Creation to Joseph
groups.blurb: The covenant of works, the fall, and the first gospel promise; God's covenant with Abraham carried through Isaac, Jacob, and Judah. Job is placed after Babel because its setting (wealth in livestock, Job offering sacrifices as head of household, long lifespan) fits the patriarchal age.

Law sections are kept to the Ten Commandments, plus Leviticus 16 because Hebrews 9 builds on it. Judges 17–21 is read near the start of the judges period because Phinehas is still serving (Judg 20:28); Ruth is placed mid-period, after Gideon.

groups.title: The Divided Kingdom and the Assyrian Age (931–c. 630 BC)
groups.blurb: Elijah and Elisha; the 8th-century prophets to the north (Jonah, Amos, Hosea) and to Judah (Isaiah, Micah); the fall of Samaria in 722 BC; Hezekiah's deliverance; and Manasseh's reign. Joel is undated and is placed in Joash's reign, a common conservative view. Isaiah 40–66 is read right after Hezekiah receives the Babylonian envoys (2 Kgs 20; Isa 39), where it sits in Isaiah, consistent with single authorship. The group ends with Nahum and Zephaniah, just before Jeremiah's call.

groups.title: Last Words: 2 Timothy, 2 Peter, Jude, John's Letters, and Revelation
groups.blurb: The final letters of Paul and Peter (c. AD 67), Jude, John's letters written late in the century, and Revelation (c. AD 95). Reformed readers have held amillennial and postmillennial views of Revelation; the notes stay neutral.
